$comment: ACCEPTED STRENGTH STATE, per lift, in Pelland Table 4 fractional sets.
Same contract as coverage-baseline.json: a gate expected to fail cannot signal a regression, so this
records what was accepted and gym-strength.mjs fails only on movement away from it.
RE-ACCEPTED 2026-09-01 for the week as it finally shipped, after his ruling on the lower back. The
sum past the point of detectable increments is 87.0, DOWN from 79.5 -> 113.0 -> 87.0 across three
states in one day. Read that arc rather than any single number, because the middle one is the
interesting one and it is now gone from the file.
79.5   the week before the rebuild
113.0  the rebuild's first version, which gave the erectors six sets of 45-degree back extension
on a catalogue claim that turned out to be false. 13.5 of the rise was that one lift
joining the priority list, and the rest was the shared-glutes mechanism: any lower-body
set raises the fractional count of every lift sharing the glutes.
87.0   the version that shipped. The back extension and the leg curl both left the prescribed
week, so both left this list, and total lower-body volume fell with them.
SO EVERY PRIORITY LIFT IS NOW AT OR BELOW WHERE IT WAS BEFORE ANY OF THIS STARTED, except the two
that were already accepted higher on 2026-09-01 for restoring the frontal-plane work. Nothing was
traded away to get there: four muscles that failed the sourced floor cleared it, and the erectors
went from 0 direct sets to 6.
A SCOPING QUESTION ABOUT THIS GATE, RECORDED AND STILL NOT FIXED HERE. `l.loadable` is read from
movements.json, so any lower-body-primary lift the catalogue calls loadable lands on a STRENGTH
table denominated per assessed exercise, whatever the programme actually prescribes. That is how a
bodyweight-prescribed back extension came to be graded as an assessed strength lift at 20.5 sets.
The same reasoning already narrowed PRIORITY_PATTERN once, on 2026-08-31, to keep calf raises and
adductor work out. It is left alone because changing a gate's scope in the commit that benefits
from the change is the move this project has been burned by. If it is fixed later, the fix belongs
on the PRESCRIPTION, not on an exercise's name: a slot marked bodyweight is not an assessed lift.
WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS THE WRONG CALL: if he reports the sessions running long. There is almost
nothing to cut. Eleven of the sixteen muscles sit at exactly two slots, so removing any block drops
one of them below the floor of 4. The only cut that costs nothing on the muscle axis is the box
jump, from five sets to three, which he has already ruled is not volume. After that the lever is
rest lengths, not blocks.
fromProgram: content/gym/program.json as shipped 2026-09-01, after his ruling on gym-lower-back-1
